presets.vless_reality_xhttp: Main one for Russia: looks like plain HTTPS and keeps few connections
presets.hysteria2: Fast on poor links, runs over UDP
presets.hysteria2_gecko: Hysteria2 whose handshake is cut into pieces of random size, against DPI that tells QUIC by packet sizes. mihomo apps on core 1.19.26+ only; the rest get plain Hysteria2
presets.tuic_v5: A QUIC alternative, also over UDP
presets.vless_reality_vision: For old clients without XHTTP. Gets frozen quickly on 443 in Russia
presets.vless_reality_grpc: HTTP/2 with multiplexing: few connections, a different traffic pattern
presets.trojan_reality: Another protocol under the same camouflage — a fallback
presets.anytls: TLS with padding against packet-size analysis; needs a mihomo or sing-box client
presets.vless_reality_xhttp_pq: XHTTP with post-quantum VLESS encryption: traffic recorded today stays sealed in the future too. Needs a recent mihomo or Xray client — sing-box apps will not connect
presets.trusttunnel: AdGuard's protocol: HTTP/2 on the node's real certificate, looks like a regular website
presets.shadowquic: QUIC that answers strangers like a real website (JLS). A spare UDP protocol
presets.mieru: Its own encryption and a random traffic pattern. TCP only
presets.shadowsocks_2022: The classic: fast and understood by every app. One key for all users
presets.sudoku: Hides traffic as HTTP and text. One key for all users
presets.snell: The Surge app's protocol. One key for all users
presets.custom: A mihomo listener template in the editor: any supported type and parameters

inbounds.subtitle: Protocols clients use to reach the server. Keys and passwords are generated automatically.
inbounds.reconnectWarning: Changing the port or camouflage reconnects this protocol's clients for a few seconds. Hysteria2 and TUIC take longer — up to 30 seconds.
inbounds.emptyText: Without them clients cannot connect. Start with VLESS REALITY XHTTP — it works best in Russia.
inbounds.deleteText: Clients using this protocol lose the connection until they switch to another one. Subscriptions update by themselves.
inbounds.errPortBusy: The port is used by another program on the server. Choose another port or free this one.
inbounds.errPermission: No permission to open this port. Check the container settings.
inbounds.newMeta: Keys, passwords and paths are generated automatically
inbounds.portHint: Default {port}/{network}. Hysteria2 accepts a range, e.g. 20000-20100.
inbounds.saved: Saved — clients get the changes when their subscription updates
inbounds.subNameHint: Clients see the connection under this name. Emoji are fine: «🇳🇱 Netherlands». Empty — the default name.
inbounds.destHint: A site with TLS 1.3 and HTTP/2, ideally in the server's network. From outside, client traffic looks like visits to this site.
inbounds.destLocked: The config was changed on the «Config» tab — change the site there too.
inbounds.destHintIP: The IP of a site next to the server: the node relays other people's probes of the port there. Outsiders see the domain below, not the IP.
inbounds.sniHint: This is the name outsiders see: clients connect as if to this site. The certificate of the site at the IP above must match it.
inbounds.sniRequired: Enter the site's domain: clients cannot connect without it
inbounds.fingerprintHint: Which browser the client looks like in the TLS handshake. If the connection gets cut, try another one.
inbounds.fingerprintLocked: The config was changed on the Config tab — change the fingerprint there (mikan.client.fingerprint).
inbounds.customMeta: A mihomo listener template: mikan fills in users, port and certificate
inbounds.configHint: mihomo listener format. name, port, listen, users and the certificate are filled in automatically. Ctrl+Space shows field hints.
inbounds.portHintCustom: A free port: TCP or UDP depends on the type in the config.
inbounds.customSkeleton:
# mihomo listener template. mikan fills in name, port, listen,
# users and the certificate. Types: vless, vmess, trojan, hysteria2, tuic, anytls.
type: trojan
ws-path: /ws
mikan:
  tls: node   # the node certificate, like Hysteria2 and TUIC
inbounds.targetScanning: Looking for sites in the server's network — up to 30 seconds…
inbounds.targetNone: No suitable sites near the server (addresses checked: {scanned}). Keep a popular site or set the server's domain in the settings to get self-steal.
inbounds.targetSelfStealHint: self-steal: the SNI matches the server's IP, the panel's Let's Encrypt certificate

targetErr.timeout: The site did not answer in time
targetErr.private: The name leads to an internal address: only public sites are checked
targetErr.sni_required: An IP needs the site's domain (SNI)
targetErr.cert: The certificate does not match the name

inbounds.nodeEmptyText: Add protocols — they appear in the subscription with the node's flag.
inbounds.autoPort: Move to another port when it is blocked
inbounds.autoPortSub: If devices reach the server's other connections but not this one, the panel moves it to a free HTTPS port.
inbounds.autoSni: Replace the camouflage site when it stops working
inbounds.autoSniSub: The node checks the site every 15 minutes. After three failures in a row it picks a working site next to the server, never its own domain.
inbounds.autoOffGlobal: Off in settings — not active now
inbounds.proxySub: If nginx stream or HAProxy holds port 443 and routes connections by SNI, the node listens on an internal address and clients go to the proxy.
inbounds.listenAllHint: The connection is open to the outside on the port above.
inbounds.listenLocalHint: Not reachable from outside: a proxy on this server forwards to {addr}.
inbounds.listenCustomHint: One IP address of this server, e.g. an internal address for a proxy on another machine.
inbounds.clientHint: Empty — as now: the node's address and the connection's port. The node keeps listening on its own port.
inbounds.clientHintReality: Empty — as now: the node's address and the connection's port. With REALITY the SNI is the camouflage site's domain: that is how the proxy tells the connection apart.
inbounds.clientPortWarn: Clients will go to port {port}, which is closed to the outside — enter the proxy's port, usually 443.
inbounds.clientLocked: The config was changed on the Config tab — change the client address there (mikan.client).
inbounds.autoPortProxy: Behind a proxy the port does not move: the proxy would not know the new one.
inbounds.autoSniProxy: If the proxy routes connections by SNI, a new site breaks the route — turn this off or update the proxy after each change.
inbounds.cutOffOf: Devices that cannot reach it: {n} of {total}

stuck.off: Automatic fixes are off for this connection.
stuck.waiting: The port or site was just changed — waiting for clients to update their subscription.
stuck.no_port: No free HTTPS ports left on the node.
stuck.no_target: No other suitable site next to the server.
stuck.exhausted: Changing the port and the site did not help: the protocol itself is probably blocked. Try another one.

inbounds.targetDown: The camouflage site does not respond: {reason}

reason.still_blocked: a new port did not help

inbounds.clashOnlyNote: Only Clash apps on a recent mihomo core get this connection: Koala Clash, SlothClash, FlClash, Clash Verge and ClashFest on Android. Happ, v2RayTun, Hiddify and others will not see it in their subscription.
inbounds.sharedWarn: The node cannot tell users apart, so per-user traffic, traffic and device limits, device binding and automatic fixes do not work here. A disabled or expired user keeps access until the key changes: to change it, delete the connection and add it again. Only users with active access get it in their subscription.
inbounds.outboundWarpHint: All traffic of this protocol leaves through the node's Cloudflare WARP: sites see a Cloudflare address. When WARP is down the traffic does not go direct — the protocol stops working until WARP is back.
inbounds.outboundNoWarp: The node has no WARP or it is off — the traffic goes direct for now. Set WARP up on the Nodes page.
inbounds.outboundNodeHint: Cascade: clients connect to this node, and the traffic leaves the internet through the chosen one — sites see its IP. When that node is down the traffic does not go direct.
inbounds.obfsHint: Every app with Hysteria2 knows Salamander. Gecko also cuts the handshake into pieces of random size, against DPI that tells QUIC by packet sizes.
inbounds.obfsGeckoHint: Only apps on mihomo core 1.19.26+ that say so (Koala Clash 1.4+, ClashFest 1.2+, SlothClash 0.9.4+ and others) get Gecko. The rest do not get this protocol, so keep a plain Hysteria2 next to it.
inbounds.portHopHint: A range such as 20000-30000 works too: clients hop between the ports, which makes blocking one port useless. Open the range over UDP in the server firewall.

settings.subtitle: Server address, subscription look and sign-in security
settings.themeSub: The panel color scheme is saved in this browser.
settings.hostHint: The IP address clients use to connect to the VPN.
settings.domainHint: Optional. When set, links use it instead of the IP.
settings.quietHourHint: Once a day at this hour the slot pool is maintained: Hysteria2 and TUIC clients briefly reconnect.
settings.subscriptionSub: How the profile looks in clients' apps
settings.brandHint: The profile gets this name in clients' apps.
settings.groupAutoHint: The group that picks the fastest connection by itself.
settings.previewHint: This is how clients see the subscription in Koala Clash and other Clash apps. Connection names are set under «Protocols».
settings.routingHint: For Koala Clash, FlClash and other mihomo apps. Happ and INCY route traffic on their own.
settings.routingRuDirectSub: Russian sites and IPs bypass the VPN by mihomo geodata: banks and state services work, and the server does not carry that traffic.
settings.routingAllSub: All traffic except the local network goes through the server.
settings.fingerprintHint: Which browser clients look like in the TLS handshake (REALITY, TLS, AnyTLS). A protocol can set its own.
settings.autoSub: The panel fixes connections that stopped working on its own
settings.autoPort: Move to another port when it is blocked
settings.autoPortSub: Devices reach the server's other connections but not one of them: its port is cut on the way. The panel moves it to a free HTTPS port: 2053, 2083, 2443…
settings.autoSni: Replace the camouflage site when it stops working
settings.autoSniSub: Every 15 minutes the node checks the REALITY camouflage site. After three failures in a row the panel picks a working site next to the server, never its own domain.
settings.autoNote: Clients get the new port or site with their next subscription update — hourly; until then the «Auto» group routes around the broken connection. Turn automatic fixes off for a single connection in its settings.
settings.updatesSub: The panel looks for releases on GitHub once a day
settings.updatesWaitingText: The server pulls the new version and restarts the panel; this page reconnects by itself. VPN pauses for a few seconds.
settings.updatesStale: The server has not taken the request in two minutes. Update on the server with mikan update: the old installer cannot update from the button.
settings.updatesAutoSub: Once a day at night. A backup first, and back to this version if the new one does not start.
settings.updatesConfirmText: The server backs up, pulls the signed release and restarts the panel and the node. VPN pauses for a few seconds. If the new version does not start, this one comes back.
settings.langSub: For visitors who have not picked a language yet
settings.langNote: The admin panel and the subscription page open in this language. Default names are in it too: the auto-select group in apps and the bot's menu until you set it up. The switch at the top of the page changes the language in this browser only.
settings.bindingSub: Each device gets keys of its own, and the device limit becomes the number of places. An extra device sees a notice that the places are taken instead of servers. Devices are listed and unbound in the user card and on the subscription page.
settings.requireHwid: Only apps with a device ID
settings.requireHwidSub: Happ, Koala Clash, INCY, v2RayTun, FlClashX and ClashFest send a device ID, and SlothClash unless it is turned off in its settings. Other apps share one place without this setting and get no subscription with it.
settings.devicesNote: A subscriber may unbind one device a day on the subscription page; you can do it any time in the user card. A device gets its own keys on the next subscription refresh.
settings.supportHint: A Telegram or website link — the «Contact support» button on the subscription page.
settings.appsSub: What subscribers see in their VPN apps besides the servers
settings.announceHint: A line over the profile in Happ, v2RayTun, ClashFest and other apps that show announcements: maintenance, news. Empty — none.
settings.announceUrlHint: Where a tap on the announcement leads: https:// or tg://
settings.appBrandingSub: ClashFest (Android) and SlothClash (Windows, macOS, Linux) show your name, logo and colour instead of their own, with links to support, the bot and renewal. Other apps ignore it.
settings.brandAccentHint: #RRGGBB. Empty — the app's own colour. A colour too pale for both themes is ignored by the app.
settings.brandLogoHint: An https link to a PNG, WebP or JPEG up to 512 KB, square, 256×256. Empty — the app's icon.
settings.adminLinkSub: Any other address on this port answers «404 Not Found».
settings.newLinkHint: If the link leaked. The old one stops working.
settings.newLinkText: The old one stops opening in a few seconds and we switch to the new one right away. Save it — without it you can only sign in through the server (mikan url).
settings.certRequested: Certificate requested — it takes up to a minute
settings.certSelf: Self-signed: browsers warn, and some apps will not accept the subscription
settings.certNote: Renews automatically. Issuance needs port 80 open — it is held for a few seconds.
settings.revokeKeys: Revoke API keys too: a key made from a hijacked session would outlive the password change
settings.newPasswordHint: At least 12 characters. A phrase of several words is handy.
settings.twoFactorOn: On: signing in needs a code from the app
settings.twoFactorOff: A code from an authenticator app at every sign-in
settings.recoveryText: Save the recovery codes — each works once if your phone is not at hand. We will not show them again.
settings.totpQr: QR code for the authenticator app
settings.totpScan: Scan the code in Google Authenticator, 1Password or Aegis and enter the 6 digits.
settings.sessionsSub: Where the panel is open now
settings.fpOwnHint: A uTLS profile name: lowercase letters, digits and _, such as chrome120 or randomizednoalpn. Xray apps may refuse a value off the list, and mihomo connects without uTLS when it does not know it.
settings.fpOwnBad: Lowercase letters, digits and _ only, up to 32 characters
settings.apiSub: Keys for scripts and integrations, and a reference of every panel method.
settings.salesSub: Plans are sold in the bot and the Mini App: Telegram Stars, YooKassa, CryptoBot.
settings.salesOnNote: Payment methods, plan prices and the history are in Payments.
settings.salesOffNote: Off: the bot and the Mini App sell nothing and Payments leaves the menu. Invoices opened before are still applied.
settings.subPortSub: Subscriptions and the subscription page on a port of their own. 443 or 2053 look like any website, and the admin panel's port stops showing in links.
settings.subPortBusy: Port {port} is taken by another program on the server, so subscriptions go through the panel's port {panel} for now. Pick another port.
settings.subPortInvalid: A port is a number from 1 to 65535
settings.subPortNote: The admin panel does not open on this port. Links on the panel's port keep working, so clients change nothing. The listed ports were opened in the firewall at install; open any other yourself if ufw is on: ufw allow PORT/tcp.
settings.rulesSub: Rules of your own for Koala Clash, FlClash, Clash Verge and other apps on mihomo. They go before the routing mode; the panel's and the nodes' addresses always go direct.
settings.rulesPlaceholder:
# One rule per line: TYPE,VALUE,TARGET
DOMAIN-SUFFIX,example.com,DIRECT
GEOSITE,youtube,PROXY
settings.rulesHint: One rule per line; lines starting with # are comments. A rule with a mistake is not saved, so it cannot break clients' profiles. Happ, v2RayTun and Hiddify get no rules: their format has none.
settings.rulesTypesText: DOMAIN, DOMAIN-SUFFIX, DOMAIN-KEYWORD, GEOSITE, GEOIP, IP-CIDR, IP-CIDR6, IP-SUFFIX, SRC-IP-CIDR, DST-PORT, SRC-PORT, NETWORK, PROCESS-NAME, PROCESS-PATH work in every mihomo app. DOMAIN-REGEX, IP-ASN, SRC-GEOIP (core 1.18+) and DOMAIN-WILDCARD (1.19.12+) reach only apps that name their core, or an older core would fail the whole profile. no-resolve is for GEOIP, IP-CIDR, IP-CIDR6, IP-SUFFIX and IP-ASN.
settings.certOwnNote: Renewed by your own tools: the panel picks a new file up without a restart.

import.title: Users from another panel
import.sub: Marzban, PasarGuard or Remnawave: users come over with their traffic limit, traffic used, term and device limit. Names mikan already has are left out.
import.urlHint: As you open it in the browser, without the admin path: https://panel.example.com. The old panel keeps working; nothing is changed there.
import.tokenHint: Remnawave → API tokens: a token with read access to users.
import.apiKeyHint: PasarGuard → API keys, with users:read. Leave empty to sign in with the username and password.
import.noLink: {n} come over without the old link: their token is too short to be a secret
import.onHold: {n} on hold: their term in mikan starts at the import, as mikan has no wait for the first connection
import.tariffHint: Users get the plan's protocols, reset strategy and pools; the limit, term and devices come from the old panel.
import.started: The import has started; you may leave the page
import.invalid: Cannot be taken as they are (too long, broken numbers): {n}
import.notCarried: Not carried over: the traffic reset strategy, groups and inbounds of the old panel (users get the plan's), and an on-hold term starts at the import. Links revoked in the old panel work again: reissue those users' links after the import.
import.skipped: {n} left out: the name is taken
import.legacySub: Point the old panel's domain at this server and set its subscription port in Settings → Subscription: the links people have keep working.
import.legacyPathHint: sub for Marzban and PasarGuard, api/sub for Remnawave (or your own). Empty: off.
import.secret: Signing secret of the old panel
import.secretHint: Marzban and PasarGuard sign every link: without their secret an old link cannot be told from a forged one, so it does not open. The secret is in the old panel's database: SELECT secret_key FROM jwt;
import.secretSet: The secret is set. Type a new one to change it.
import.legacyCount: Old links and users on file: {n}

sub.loadFailedText: Check your internet and reload the page. If it does not help, contact whoever gave you the link.

status.limited: Traffic for this period has run out

sub.devicesFull: All places are taken. To connect a new device, unbind one you no longer use.
sub.devicesEmpty: Devices appear here once an app loads the subscription.
sub.devicesNote: Each device takes one place. An unbound device is disconnected at once. You can unbind one device a day.
sub.unbindWarn: The device disconnects at once and its place frees up.
sub.unbindAfter: You can unbind the next device on {date} at {time}
sub.unbindFailed: Couldn't unbind. Reload the page and try again.

sub.tgNoSubText: Open your subscription link in a browser and tap “Open in Telegram”, or send the link to the bot.
sub.tgFailed: Could not sign in with Telegram. Close the page and open it again.
sub.tgBrowser: A browser opens, then the app
sub.shopDone: Once paid, the subscription updates by itself and the bot messages you.
sub.shopFail: Could not open the payment. Try again or message support.
sub.shopNotForSale: This plan is no longer sold.
sub.shopTooMany: Too many invoices in a row — try again in an hour.
sub.shopTooManySubs: The account already holds the most subscriptions it can.
sub.promoRefundUnsupported: This payment method cannot refund an expired promo payment. Choose another method.
sub.poolOut: Used up — these servers come back after the traffic resets.
sub.packagesPick: Pick a package: it adds to the plan's traffic
sub.packageNotForSale: This package is no longer sold.
sub.promoHint: Redeem bonuses here; discounts are checked at checkout.
sub.promoDiscountApplied: Code saved. The discount will be checked at checkout.
sub.promoUnavailable: Could not redeem the promo code
sub.promoTryLater: Too many promo attempts. Try again in 15 minutes.
sub.promoInactive: Promo code is not active yet
sub.promoUserLimit: This promo code has already been used

nodes.subtitle: Servers that run the VPN. The subscription includes the protocols of every enabled node, each in its own group.
nodes.emptyText: The panel's own node appears here once it starts.
nodes.localOffline: The panel cannot see its own node. Check on the server: mikan status.
nodes.remoteOffline: The panel cannot reach the node. If it was just added, install it with the command from its key; otherwise check that the server is up and the API port is open.
nodes.rekeyText: The old key stops working at once: the node is disconnected until mikan join runs on its server with the new key.
nodes.deleteText: The node stops serving clients and its protocols leave the subscriptions. To clean up the server itself, run mikan uninstall on it.
nodes.newMeta: A server that will serve VPN for this panel
nodes.name: Name
nodes.nameHint: The group in the subscription. A leading flag prefixes its protocol names: «🇺🇸 VLESS XHTTP».
nodes.publicNameHint: Optional. Fill this in to include the node in the public status; users will see this name.
nodes.hostHint: The panel connects to the node at this address, and clients connect to its protocols.
nodes.domainHint: Optional. Used instead of the IP in Hysteria2 and TUIC links.
nodes.apiPortHint: The panel connects to the node on this port over key-checked TLS.
nodes.keyOnce: The key is shown once. If you lose it, issue a new one on the node's card.
nodes.keyStep1: Run the command below on the node's server as root: the installer sets up Docker and the node and opens its ports.
nodes.keyStep2: In half a minute the node shows up here as «Working».
nodes.localAddress: The own node's address is the panel's address; change it in the settings.
nodes.servingHint: A disabled node accepts no connections and leaves the subscriptions.
nodes.nameLocalHint: Name your own node with a flag, e.g. «🇳🇱 Netherlands»: that is its group in the subscription, and the flag prefixes its protocols.

telegram.subtitle: A bot for subscription owners and a Mini App with the subscription page
telegram.leaveText: Changes to the bot's menu, texts and options are not saved yet and will be lost.
telegram.connectSub: The bot runs inside the panel, no separate server needed
telegram.miniAppNoCert: The Mini App works once the panel has a Let's Encrypt certificate: Telegram will not open a page on a self-signed one
telegram.step1: Create a bot with @BotFather using /newbot and copy its token.
telegram.step2: Paste the token below: the panel checks it with Telegram.
telegram.tokenHint: Looks like 123456789:AAH… The panel does not show it after saving.
telegram.removeText: The bot stops answering. Subscription links stay: with a new token everything works as before.

err.token_invalid: Telegram refused the token: check it with @BotFather
err.token_revoked: The token was revoked in @BotFather: paste a new one
err.unreachable: Telegram is unreachable: the bot will reconnect by itself. If Telegram is blocked on the server, send the bot through a node or a proxy in “Way to Telegram”.
err.route_invalid: The way to Telegram does not work: check the node or the proxy in “Way to Telegram”.

telegram.menuSub: Buttons under the bot's message. A press changes that message instead of sending a new one
telegram.sameRow: same row as the previous one

action.connect: How to connect: link and subscription page
action.app: Mini App with the subscription page

telegram.textsSub: An empty field uses the built-in text (shown in grey)
telegram.langHint: The language of built-in words and dates. Button labels are edited in the menu above
telegram.optionsSub: Each notice comes once per term or traffic period
telegram.miniAppSub: The subscription page opens right in Telegram, without a browser
telegram.cleanChat: Keep one menu in the chat
telegram.cleanChatSub: The bot deletes the user's messages and its previous menu: the chat stays clean
telegram.quietNightSub: From 22:00 to 9:00 Moscow time, subscription notices arrive without a sound so nobody is woken up
telegram.broadcastSub: A message to everyone with a subscription in the bot: {n}
telegram.broadcastPlaceholder: E.g. maintenance tonight, short breaks possible
telegram.broadcastHint: Plain text, {brand} is filled in. Up to 20 messages a second; replies in the bot skip the queue
telegram.broadcastOff: Turn the bot on to send
telegram.broadcastFailed: {n} not delivered: the bot is blocked or the chat is gone
telegram.routeSub: When Telegram is blocked on the panel's server, the bot can reach it through a node in another country or through a proxy.
telegram.routeDirectHint: Requests leave from the panel's server. Fine where Telegram is open.
telegram.routeNodeHint: A remote node of the panel in a country where Telegram is open. The node passes only requests to Telegram; it needs 0.4.2 or later.
telegram.routeNoNodes: No remote nodes: connect a server in another country on the Nodes page.
telegram.routeProxyHint: SOCKS5 or HTTP(S): socks5://login:password@host:port. The password stays in the panel and is not shown again.
telegram.routeProxyKeep: Saved: {proxy}. Leave the field empty to keep it.

infra.title: Infrastructure status
infra.subtitle: Private alerts for the admin and a public status for users
infra.adminHint: Outages and recoveries are sent to your private chat with the bot.
infra.linkHint: Open the bot with this one-time link to verify your chat.
infra.publicHint: Make the bot a channel admin with permission to post, edit and pin messages.
infra.summaryHint: The bot creates and updates one message with the status of published nodes.
infra.changesHint: Separate messages when a node moves to another status.
infra.events: Events to send to the admin
infra.eventsHint: Outage alerts also include recovery notices.
infra.eventAutotuneRecovery: Autotune could not restore a connection
infra.backupSub: Once a day the panel's database (users, plans, settings) goes to the admin chat, encrypted with your password. The server's .env, certificates and node keys stay on the server: keep the host's own backups for those.
infra.backupNoChat: Connect the admin chat above: backups go there.
infra.backupPasswordSet: A password is set. Type a new one to change it.
infra.backupPasswordHint: At least 20 characters, or press Generate. Every file stays in the chat's history for good, so a short phrase could be guessed offline. Keep it outside the server: without it a backup does not open, and nobody can recover it.
infra.backupKeepIt: Save this password somewhere outside the server now (a password manager). It is not shown again, and without it no backup opens.
infra.backupStarted: The backup is being made; it will be in the chat in a minute

apiPage.title: API
apiPage.subtitle: Keys for scripts and integrations, and the panel's API reference.
apiPage.keysSub: A script with a key acts on your behalf. Revoke a key if it may have leaked.
apiPage.noKeysText: Create a key so a bot, billing or monitoring can work with the panel without signing in.
apiPage.scopeReadHint: GET requests only: users, statistics, settings. No subscription links or secret addresses.
apiPage.scopeFullHint: Changes: create and extend users, edit tariffs and inbounds. Not sign-in, sessions, keys or operations that move money, keys and client addresses: payments, Telegram, nodes, updates, the panel address.
apiPage.passwordHint: A key is made only with the password: a stolen session cannot leave a key behind.
apiPage.revokeText: Scripts with this key stop working at once. This cannot be undone.
apiPage.name: Name
apiPage.nameHint: To remember where the key is used.
apiPage.madeOnce: Copy the key now: the panel keeps only its fingerprint and will not show it again.
apiPage.startSub: REST and JSON. The reference below is built from this panel version's code.
apiPage.authKey: Scripts send the key in the header Authorization: Bearer mk_…
apiPage.authScopes: A Read key runs GET only and does not see subscription links. Full access works with users, tariffs and inbounds; sign-in, keys, 2FA, the panel's addresses, nodes, certificates, WARP, payments, the bot and updates change only in the admin panel.
apiPage.authSession: In the browser the API works with the admin session; changing requests then need X-CSRF-Token from GET /auth/me.
apiPage.errorsFormat: Errors follow RFC 9457: detail holds the error code, errors[].message the code per field.
apiPage.secret: The address holds the panel's secret path — do not publish it together with a key.
apiPage.referenceSub: {n} methods with parameters, responses and examples
apiPage.nothingFoundText: Try part of a path, such as users or inbounds.
apiPage.errorsShort: Errors: application/problem+json with the code in detail.
apiPage.tryItHint: The request goes with your session; GET changes nothing.
apiPage.downloadHint: openapi.json for Postman, Insomnia, Swagger UI and client generators. It carries this panel's address, which is secret: do not publish the file.
apiPage.prometheusHint: GET /metrics gives users by state, users online, traffic, nodes, their load and protocols in the Prometheus format. Scrape it with a read key; this is the job for prometheus.yml:

payments.title: Payments
payments.subtitle: Plans paid for in the bot and the Mini App: subscriptions are issued and renewed by themselves.
payments.notApplied: Not applied: {error}. The panel retries every minute.
payments.emptyText: Turn a payment method on and mark plans “On sale”.
payments.refundText: The Stars go back to the buyer. The subscription stays as it is — turn it off in the user card if needed.
payments.settingsSub: Keys stay in the panel and are never shown again.
payments.starsSub: Payment inside Telegram, no keys — only the running bot.
payments.starsBotOff: The bot is not running: turn it on on the Telegram tab.
payments.keySaved: Saved — enter a new one to replace it
payments.webhookNoHost: The address appears once the panel has a domain or IP.
payments.allowNewSub: Someone without a subscription can buy one in the bot. Off: renewals only.
payments.resetTrafficOn: A paid renewal starts a new period: the used traffic goes back to zero.
payments.resetTrafficOff: A paid renewal only adds time: the traffic counter runs on as before.
payments.trialSub: A “Try it for free” button in the bot's welcome: a subscription on the plan picked, once per Telegram account that has had no subscription or payment. Works with selling off too.
payments.nothingOnSale: The bot sells nothing yet: no plan is on sale with a price for a method that takes payments. Instead of buying, people are told to message support.
payments.salesOff: Selling is off: the bot and the Mini App sell nothing. Payment methods can be set up beforehand.
payments.rublesInMarketplace: Rubles (YooKassa, CryptoBot and more) are set up below, in Payment methods from the marketplace.
payments.moving: YooKassa and CryptoBot moved to the marketplace and their keys came along. The server is installing the adapter ({names}): it takes no payments until then.

warp.title: WARP
warp.intro: Cloudflare WARP is a second way out to the internet for the node. The protocols and domains you pick leave through WARP: sites see a Cloudflare address instead of the server's. It helps when the server's IP routes badly or some sites block it.
warp.registerHint: The panel creates a free WARP account at Cloudflare, the way the WARP app does.
warp.licenseHint: Optional. The key from the 1.1.1.1 app → Account → Key.
warp.confHint: From wgcf, warp-plus or the app's export. The private key stays in the panel and goes only to the node.
warp.ready: WARP is set up — pick the protocols that use it
warp.downText: The node could not reach the internet through WARP — no traffic goes through it now
warp.nodeUnreachable: The node did not answer — the state shows once it is reachable
warp.enabledSub: Turn off to send all traffic direct for a while — the account and lists stay.
warp.inboundsHint: Picked in a protocol's settings: “Way out to the internet → WARP”.
warp.routesHint: For every protocol of the node. One per line: example.com with its subdomains, 104.16.0.0/13 for a network.
warp.deleteText: All traffic of the node goes direct. The account is removed from the panel; protocols set to WARP stay so but work direct.

cascade.title: Cascade
cascade.intro: A cascade is a chain of servers: client → this node → another node → internet. Clients connect to the near node, sites see the far one. No WARP needed.
cascade.exits: This node sends traffic out through
cascade.exitsNone: Nothing yet: everything leaves from here.
cascade.exitsHint: The exit node is picked in a protocol's settings: “Way out to the internet → Via a node”.
cascade.relay: Other nodes' traffic through this one
cascade.sources: Leaving through this node: {list}. The relay listens on {port}/tcp.
cascade.sourcesNone: No node leaves through this one yet. Once one does, the panel opens the relay itself.
cascade.route: Where other nodes' traffic goes next

routeHint.direct: To the internet from this server.
routeHint.warp: Through this node's WARP — WARP must be set up.
routeHint.node: Further down the chain, through one more node.

pools.title: Traffic pools
pools.sub: A separate limit for some protocols: say, a WL node at 100 GB a month while the rest stay unlimited. A pool's traffic does not use the main limit.
pools.none: No pools yet — all traffic counts to the main limit.
pools.empty: No protocols: pick the pool in a protocol's settings
pools.name: Pool name
pools.deleteText: Its protocols go back to the main traffic, the pool's limits in plans and users are dropped, and traffic packages for the pool are deleted with what is left of them.
pools.hint: A protocol joins a pool in its own settings: “Traffic pool”. The pool's limit is set in the plan and per user.
pools.inboundHint: This protocol's traffic counts to the pool with its own limit, not to the main one. When the pool runs out, only it stops.
pools.tariffLimitsHint: GB for the same period as the main traffic. Empty — unlimited.
pools.errLimit: A limit is a positive number of GB, or empty
pools.exhausted: Used up: the pool's protocols are off until the reset
pools.drawerMeta: A limit of its own for some protocols
pools.nameHint: Subscribers see it in the bot and on the subscription page.

cert.panelLead: Instead of Let's Encrypt: a wildcard from certbot over DNS, a Cloudflare Origin certificate or your own CA's. Port 80 is not needed then.
cert.panelClearText: The panel gets a Let's Encrypt certificate again (port 80 needed) and keeps the own one until then.
cert.nodeLead: For the protocols on the node's certificate: Hysteria2, TUIC, AnyTLS, TrustTunnel. Apps accept a publicly trusted one without a pin, so renewing it breaks nothing.
cert.nodeClearText: The node goes back to its self-signed certificate; clients get its pin with the next subscription refresh.
cert.soon: {n, plural, one {# day left} other {# days left}}
cert.chainHint: fullchain.pem: the certificate first, then the intermediates.
cert.keyHint: privkey.pem. It stays in the panel and is never shown again.
cert.tooBig: Larger than 64 KB: not a certificate or a key
cert.cliHint: Renewing with certbot or acme.sh? Run this on the server on renewal and the panel picks the new file up:

addons.title: Payment methods from the marketplace
addons.sub: Payment adapters from the signed getmikan/marketplace catalog, installed on this server as containers of their own.
addons.unsupported: The panel cannot see the server's data directory: adapters are installed only by the mikan installer.
addons.emptyText: Press Add to connect a payment provider from the marketplace.
addons.unreachable: The adapter does not answer, its settings are unavailable. On the server: mikan addon list
addons.requested: The request went to the server
addons.removeText: The adapter's container stops and payments through it are no longer offered. Its settings and payment history stay: installing it again brings everything back.
addons.webhook: Notification URL for the provider's dashboard:
addons.catalogEmptyText: No adapters for this panel version yet.

packages.title: Traffic packages
packages.sub: Extra traffic on top of the plan, for the main limit or a pool. The plan's traffic is spent first, then the packages, the one that expires sooner first.
packages.none: No packages yet. A package can be sold in the bot and the Mini App or given by hand in a user's card.
